concept.name: Feature selection
concept.definition: Choosing a subset of candidate inputs using prespecified statistical, model-based, or domain criteria.
concept.intuition: It estimates how a fitted choice behaves on observations that were not used to fit that choice.
concept.mechanics: Fit the selector inside each training fold, apply it to that fold's validation data, and repeat selection when the training window changes.
concept.failure_modes: Random splitting, overlapping labels, repeated tuning, or an unprotected final test set can produce optimistic estimates.
concept.misconceptions: Validation measures conditional generalization under a split design; it does not guarantee future market performance.
concept.example: Within each fold, the 10 highest training-set mutual-information features are selected from 200 candidates.
